name: settings
note: A long list under a nav bar — the shape most likely to have content misfiled as chrome.

name: browser
note: A static page, so its structure should be identical on every visit. Arrival is asserted on a CHROME control and not only on the page text: "Example Domain" is page content that OCR alone can satisfy, so the tour used to proceed while Safari's accessibility tree was still empty on a cold first launch. Measured — sharding CI removed the memory-layer step that had been warming Safari, and round 1 then read e00725fce7 with 0 named elements where rounds 2 and 3 read 9589eb2471 with 5. Waiting for "Address", which only the tree can name, makes arrival mean addressable rather than merely drawn.

name: reminders
note: A near-empty list. Structurally sparse, which is where two screens are most likely to look alike.

name: contacts
note: An indexed list with a search field — a nav bar with two rows in it.

name: settings-general
note: With the next screen, the case chrome labels exist for: two lists under a nav bar with near-identical structure, told apart by their title and nothing else. Without a nav title in the fingerprint these collide.

name: settings-accessibility
note: The other half of that pair. Arrival waits for EITHER "VoiceOver" or "Display & Text Size", because VoiceOver is not reliably above the fold: on a runner's iOS the Accessibility screen read Settings, Accessibility, Vision, Hover Text, Display & Text Size, Motion, Spoken Content … Hearing, with no VoiceOver on it at all, and the tour waited 8000ms for something below the scroll. The two landmarks in this entry's own `intents` were in that list the whole time — the arrival test was asking for a label the entry itself did not rely on.
